patches.old:
The virgins carried the stones in the positions they had taken around the gate. Those who seemed strong went under the stone’s corners. The others went under its sides. This was how they carried every stone. They brought them through the gate as ordered and handed them to the men at the tower. The men took them and built with them.

2. The tower was built on the great rock and above the gate. The ten stones were fitted together. They filled the whole rock and became the tower’s foundation. The rock and the gate supported the whole tower.[a]

3. After the ten stones, twenty-five more came up from the depth.[b] The virgins carried them like the first ones, and they were fitted into the tower’s building. Next came thirty-five, which were fitted into the tower in the same way. Then forty more came up. All were put into the building. These made four courses in the tower’s foundations.[c]

4. Stones stopped rising from the depth. The builders paused briefly. The six men again told the crowd to bring stones from the mountains for the tower’s building.

5. The men cut stones of different colors from all the mountains and handed them to the virgins. The virgins carried them through the gate and handed them over for the tower’s building. Once placed in the building, the different stones all became white and alike. Their varied colors changed.

6. The men handed some stones into the building themselves. These did not become bright. They stayed as they had been when put there. The virgins had not handed them over or carried them through the gate. These stones looked out of place in the tower’s building.[d]

7. The six men saw the stones that looked out of place. They ordered them removed and taken down to the place they came from.[e]

8. They told the men bringing stones, “Do not hand stones into the building yourselves. Put them beside the tower. Let the virgins carry them through the gate and hand them into the building. The stones cannot change color unless these virgins carry them through the gate. So do not work in vain.”[f]

translation:
  text: 'Just as they had stood together around the gate, so they carried the stones. Those who seemed
    strong had gone under the corners of the stone; the others had gone under its sides. In this way they
    carried all the stones. They brought them through the gate as commanded and handed them to the men
    at the tower. The men took the stones and built with them.


    2. The tower was built on the great rock and above the gate. Those ten stones were fitted together,
    filled the whole rock, and became the foundation of the tower’s building. The rock and the gate supported
    the whole tower.[a]


    3. After the ten stones, another twenty-five stones came up from the depth.[b] These too were fitted
    into the tower’s building, carried by the virgins like the first ones. After these, thirty-five came
    up and were fitted into the tower in the same way. After these, another forty stones came up. All
    were put into the tower’s building. Thus there were four courses in the tower’s foundations.[c]


    4. Then stones stopped rising from the depth, and the builders paused briefly. Again the six men ordered
    the crowd to bring stones from the mountains for the tower’s building.


    5. Stones of various colors were brought from all the mountains. The men cut them and handed them
    to the virgins. The virgins carried them through the gate and handed them over for the tower’s building.
    When the variously colored stones were placed in the building, they became alike and white, changing
    their varied colors.


    6. Some stones were handed into the building by the men and did not become bright. They were found
    just as they had been when placed there, for they had not been handed over by the virgins or brought
    through the gate. So these stones looked out of place in the tower’s building.[d]


    7. When the six men saw the stones that looked out of place, they ordered them removed and taken down
    to their own place, from which they had been brought.[e]


    8. They said to the men bringing the stones, “Do not hand any stones into the building yourselves.
    Put them beside the tower so that the virgins may carry them through the gate and hand them into the
    building. Unless they are brought through the gate by these virgins’ hands, they cannot change their
    colors. So do not toil in vain.”[f]'

translation:
  text: 'The virgins carried the stones in the positions they had taken around the gate. Those who seemed
    strong went under the stone’s corners. The others went under its sides. This was how they carried
    every stone. They brought them through the gate as ordered and handed them to the men at the tower.
    The men took them and built with them.


    2. The tower was built on the great rock and above the gate. The ten stones were fitted together.
    They filled the whole rock and became the tower’s foundation. The rock and the gate supported the
    whole tower.[a]


    3. After the ten stones, twenty-five more came up from the depth.[b] The virgins carried them like
    the first ones, and they were fitted into the tower’s building. Next came thirty-five, which were
    fitted into the tower in the same way. Then forty more came up. All were put into the building. These
    made four courses in the tower’s foundations.[c]


    4. Stones stopped rising from the depth. The builders paused briefly. The six men again told the crowd
    to bring stones from the mountains for the tower’s building.


    5. The men cut stones of different colors from all the mountains and handed them to the virgins. The
    virgins carried them through the gate and handed them over for the tower’s building. Once placed in
    the building, the different stones all became white and alike. Their varied colors changed.


    6. The men handed some stones into the building themselves. These did not become bright. They stayed
    as they had been when put there. The virgins had not handed them over or carried them through the
    gate. These stones looked out of place in the tower’s building.[d]


    7. The six men saw the stones that looked out of place. They ordered them removed and taken down to
    the place they came from.[e]


    8. They told the men bringing stones, “Do not hand stones into the building yourselves. Put them beside
    the tower. Let the virgins carry them through the gate and hand them into the building. The stones
    cannot change color unless these virgins carry them through the gate. So do not work in vain.”[f]'

  text: 'Just as they had stood together around the gate, so they carried the stones. Those who seemed
    strong had gone under the corners of the stone; the others had gone under its sides. In this way they
    carried all the stones. They brought them through the gate as commanded and handed them to the men
    at the tower. The men took the stones and built with them.


    2. The tower was built on the great rock and above the gate. Those ten stones were fitted together,
    filled the whole rock, and became the foundation of the tower’s building. The rock and the gate supported
    the whole tower.[a]


    3. After the ten stones, another twenty-five stones came up from the depth.[b] These too were fitted
    into the tower’s building, carried by the virgins like the first ones. After these, thirty-five came
    up and were fitted into the tower in the same way. After these, another forty stones came up. All
    were put into the tower’s building. Thus there were four courses in the tower’s foundations.[c]


    4. Then stones stopped rising from the depth, and the builders paused briefly. Again the six men ordered
    the crowd to bring stones from the mountains for the tower’s building.


    5. Stones of various colors were brought from all the mountains. The men cut them and handed them
    to the virgins. The virgins carried them through the gate and handed them over for the tower’s building.
